evidence.description:
Lon Mitchell performs on the Ann & Robert H. Lurie Carillon, an instrument of 60 bells with the lowest bell (bourdon) weighing 6 tons.

Thirty-minute recitals are performed on the Lurie Carillon every weekday that classes are in session. During these recitals, visitors may take the elevator to level 2 to view the largest bells, or to level 3 to see the carillonist performing. (Visitors subject to acrophobia are recommended to visit level 2 only.) An optional spiral stairway between levels 2 and 3 allows for up-close views of some of the largest bells.

events.title: Learning Seminar in Algebraic Combinatorics
events.summary: Attend a seminar on algebraic combinatorics exploring torus-equivariant cohomology classes of smooth projective varieties. The session will delve into the 6-vertex model and its relation to Schubert classes and R-matrices for flag varieties.
events.experienceId: experience:["ann arbor","east hall","learning seminar in algebraic combinatorics"]

evidence.description: Torus-equivariant cohomology classes of smooth projective varieties (e.g. flag varieties) are determined by their restrictions to fixed points. We'll compute these for Schubert classes in type A, using the 5-vertex model and colored extensions. The 6-vertex will be about the "Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson" deformations of Schubert classes. Then we'll introduce a trivalent analogue of R-matrices and use it to compute the products of Schubert classes, for up to 4-step flag varieties.
